blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Culture transformation is one of the most misunderstood undertakings in management. Executives often believe that, if they can articulate the desired values clearly enough and communicate them broadly enough, culture will follow. Culture, however, does not follow words — it follows decisions.

Real culture change happens when leaders systematically alter what gets rewarded, what gets promoted, which behaviours are tolerated, and which are confronted in public. It happens when a senior executive who delivers the numbers but damages trust is removed — and everyone in the company notices. Such moments do more for culture than any number of townhalls or posters.

It is, admittedly, a slow and uncomfortable process. Leaders often do want a better culture, but they underestimate how much personal behaviour and how many difficult decisions it demands of them. What they hope for is a programme that will quietly shift the organisation while leaving their own habits untouched. That is not culture change — that is culture wallpaper.

items.q: According to the text, culture ultimately follows…
items.why: "Culture, however, does not follow words — it follows decisions."

items.q: What does the removal of a senior executive who damages trust achieve, according to the text?
options: It does more for culture than townhalls or posters
It slows down the transformation programme
items.why: "Such moments do more for culture than any number of townhalls or posters."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Rewarding the wrong behaviours undermines any values programme.
Real change forces leaders to alter their own behaviour.
What leaders tolerate signals what they endorse.
A well-communicated values statement is enough to change a culture.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro é um argumento contra a ideia de que comunicar valores, por si só, muda a cultura.

items.q: The term "culture wallpaper" suggests that some programmes…
options: decorate the organisation without changing anything real
move too quickly for leaders to follow
items.why: Inferência: papel de parede cobre a superfície sem alterar a estrutura — muda a aparência, não o comportamento.

items.q: What does "leaving their own habits untouched" imply leaders are hoping to avoid?
options: Changing themselves as part of the process
items.why: Inferência: eles querem transformar a organização sem pagar o custo pessoal de mudar o próprio comportamento.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie desafiando o comitê executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, I'm going to say the thing everyone in this room is thinking but nobody will put on the record. We all know exactly which leader I mean. He delivers the numbers, quarter after quarter — and he leaves a trail of burnt-out people and broken trust behind him.

Every one of us has signed off on the values on that wall. Respect. Candour. Care. And every one of us has watched him breach all three, in public, for two years. The whole organisation is watching too. They are not reading our posters; they are reading what we tolerate.

So let me be blunt. If we confirm his promotion next week, we are not endorsing his results — we are endorsing his behaviour. And every high performer beneath him will learn, correctly, that trust is optional here as long as you hit target.

I am not asking us to pretend the numbers don't matter. I am asking whether we have the nerve to confront him, or whether we quietly decide, one more time, that we don't. There is no neutral vote here. Doing nothing is a decision — and it is the loudest one we could possibly make.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Sophie's central concern about the leader in question?
options: He hits his numbers but damages trust and people
He communicates the values too aggressively
He is too junior for the promotion
He fails to deliver his commercial targets
items.why: "He delivers the numbers… and he leaves a trail of burnt-out people and broken trust behind him."

items.q: According to Sophie, what is the whole organisation actually reading?
items.why: "They are not reading our posters; they are reading what we tolerate."

items.q: What does Sophie say confirming his promotion would really endorse?
items.why: "we are not endorsing his results — we are endorsing his behaviour."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "There is no neutral vote here"?
options: Inaction is itself a decision that endorses his behaviour
Only Sophie is allowed to decide
The vote should be postponed until next quarter
items.why: Inferência: para Sophie, não confrontar equivale a aprovar — o silêncio é uma escolha ativa.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
options: Direct and morally challenging, but not dismissive of results
items.why: Inferência: ela é frontal e cobra coragem moral, mas admite explicitamente que os números importam.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board finally committed to a genuine culture transformation." This refers to…
options: a deep, organisation-wide change in how people actually behave
a rebranding of the company logo
items.why: Culture transformation = transformação cultural: mudança profunda no comportamento coletivo, não cosmética.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The problem is not what leaders say, but what they are willing to ___ when values are breached."
items.why: To tolerate = tolerar; o que a liderança tolera define a cultura real.

items.q: "Nobody was prepared to confront him about his conduct." To confront means to…
options: challenge or address the behaviour directly
items.why: To confront = confrontar: encarar e tratar o problema de frente, não evitá-lo.

items.q: Tone at the top is best described as…
options: the example set by senior leadership through their own behaviour
the design of the executive offices
the seniority of the newest hires
items.why: Tone at the top = o exemplo da liderança: o comportamento dos executivos que a organização imita.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Real change demands ___ — leaders answering personally for their own conduct, not just the team's."
items.why: Personal accountability = responsabilização pessoal: o líder responde pela própria conduta.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre cultura e liderança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on his promotion." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on confronting the leader." They…
options: resisted or objected to the idea
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — opor-se sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Leadership announced the values but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry the commitment to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Another poster campaign won't move the needle on trust." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.

items.q: "By staying silent, the committee effectively turned a blind eye to his conduct." They…
options: reported it to the board at once
deliberately ignored something they knew was wrong
items.why: Turn a blind eye to = fazer vista grossa: ignorar de propósito algo errado que se conhece.
